eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus at 100% on 12°C reflects official forecasts from Argentina’s Servicio Meteorológico Nacional and international models projecting a daily maximum of 11–12°C under stable high-pressure conditions (1026–1028 hPa) with easterly flow and mostly cloudy skies.** 

Current observations show afternoon temperatures peaking near 10–11°C, consistent with suppressed mixing and seasonal late-winter patterns where August averages run cooler than the long-term high of ~15–18°C. The market-implied odds capture this tight clustering around the expected peak, with negligible probability assigned to deviations. 

A realistic challenge would require unexpected solar heating from rapid clearing or a wind shift that allows readings to reach 13°C at official stations before sunset, though model consensus and ongoing observations make this unlikely.

eventMetadata.context_description: A recent influx of cooler maritime air and increased cloud cover from southeasterly flow has suppressed daytime heating in São Paulo ahead of August 24. Official and ensemble forecasts from sources such as the Met Office, Yr, and regional models converge on a maximum of 18–21 °C under mostly cloudy to overcast skies, with only limited solar insolation and possible light drizzle. This follows a sharp cooldown from mid-month highs near 30 °C, placing the day well below late-August climatological normals of 22–24 °C. Model spread centers on cloud thickness and any brief afternoon clearing, keeping the highest temperature tightly clustered around 19–21 °C and explaining the near-even market probabilities for those outcomes. Updated model runs and official briefings through the evening of August 23 will refine the final range.

Recent cooling from widespread rainfall has kept readings below seasonal averages, creating tight trader consensus around 19–20°C as the most likely outcomes. Updated model runs and surface observations on the 23rd reinforce this narrow range, with limited warming potential before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Jinnah International Airport in degrees Celsius on 25 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=opkc

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current model consensus from PAGASA and international forecasters points to a daily maximum of 30–32°C in Manila on August 25 under southwest monsoon flow, which favors scattered thunderstorms and persistent cloud cover that limit solar heating and cap afternoon peaks. High humidity near 80% and moderate southwesterly winds further moderate temperatures while increasing the likelihood of brief rain episodes that can shave 1–2°C off the high. Historical August averages hover near 31°C, providing context for why market-implied odds cluster tightly around 31°C (30%) and 32°C (27.5%), with lower probabilities assigned to outliers that would require unusually clear skies or stronger subsidence. PAGASA’s next regional update and any revised model runs over the next 48 hours remain the key near-term catalysts for shifts in trader positioning ahead of the official observation used for resolution.
